losses.comment: Thu 1 Oct, 11:18 PKT. At 11:00-11:02 PKT a spike lifted EUR/USD 7 pips (1.1318 to 1.1325) on 251/190/154-tick candles. The retracement was only 1.6 pips (extreme 1.13229), and the buy filled at 1.13248: 0.2-0.4 pip under that ceiling, the sixth test of it, with the camel just turned GREEN x1. That fill was the high of the next 73 minutes. The flag broke down and ran to the stop at 1.1304. What was visible before entry: a flat-topped flag after a spike, and a buy right under equal highs. It does not separate. Both twins (10:43 and 10:48 buys at 1.13207-09) also bought within 0.5 pip of small tops (10:38 high 1.13212), and both won. As a rule, 'swing high 0-0.6 pip ahead' (ceiling_just_ahead) removes 96 losers and 4,434 winners (lift 0.94). No selective rule catches this one.
losses.cause: into resistance (flat-top flag after a spike)

rules.idea: Friday after 16:00 New York (last hour of the week): a round still open at the 16:58 NY weekly close is force-closed at a loss.
rules.code:
def rule(t, A):
    """Friday after 16:00 New York (20:00 UTC in summer): the last hour of the week."""
    ts = t["t_in"]
    x = ts + (-4 * 3600 if 1772953200 <= ts < 1793512800 else -5 * 3600)
    dow, hr = int(((x // 86400) + 3) % 7), (x % 86400) / 3600.0
    return dow == 4 and hr >= 16.0
rules.verdict: EXCELLENT (but 8 of its 11 losers are forced weekly-close exits, why=8: depends on the MT5 EA flattening at the close like the sim)

def rule(t, A):
    """Friday after 14:00 New York (18:00 UTC in summer, 19:00 UTC in winter): the last 3 hours of the week. Liquidity drains, and a round
    still open at the weekly close (16:58 NY) is closed there at a loss."""
    ts = t["t_in"]
    x = ts + (-4 * 3600 if 1772953200 <= ts < 1793512800 else -5 * 3600)
    dow, hr = int(((x // 86400) + 3) % 7), (x % 86400) / 3600.0          # dow 0 = Monday
    return dow == 4 and hr >= 14.0
rules.verdict: EXCELLENT (14 of 18 losers are weekly-close exits; beyond the existing 20:45-21:15 UTC band it fails test, 1.46 - see fri14_beyond_noclose_band)

def rule(t, A):
    """Friday 16:45-17:00 New York: the last 15 minutes before the weekly close - the round cannot even finish."""
    ts = t["t_in"]
    x = ts + (-4 * 3600 if 1772953200 <= ts < 1793512800 else -5 * 3600)

    return dow == 4 and hr >= 16.75

rules.idea: Sun-Thu 16:45-18:00 New York (20:45-22:00 UTC in summer), incl. Sunday's weekly-open hour: the daily rollover - spreads blow out, book is thin, a break is a quote wobble.
rules.code:
def rule(t, A):
    """Sunday-Thursday 16:45-18:00 New York (20:45-22:00 UTC in summer), incl. Sunday's weekly-open hour: the daily rollover - the broker's
    day break, spreads blow out and the book is thin; a 'breakout' there is a quote wobble, not a move."""
    ts = t["t_in"]
    x = ts + (-4 * 3600 if 1772953200 <= ts < 1793512800 else -5 * 3600)
    dow, hr = int(((x // 86400) + 3) % 7), (x % 86400) / 3600.0
    return dow in (0, 1, 2, 3, 6) and 16.75 <= hr < 18.0
rules.verdict: GOOD (all 8 removed losers are real 20-pip stop-outs, why=1)

rules.idea: THE CLOCK RULE: Friday after 14:00 NY OR the daily rollover 16:45-18:00 NY (Sun-Thu). New York time, so it follows US DST.
rules.verdict: EXCELLENT (the recommended clock rule; 12 of its 26 losers are stop-outs, 14 weekly-close exits)

rules.idea: fri_after_14ny minus the engine's existing InpUhvNoClose band (20:45-21:15 UTC daily, off in this setting): what it adds beyond the switch Zee has.
rules.code:
def rule(t, A):
    """What fri_after_14ny adds BEYOND the engine's existing InpUhvNoClose band (20:45-21:15 UTC every day, api's example)."""
    ts = t["t_in"]
    x = ts + (-4 * 3600 if 1772953200 <= ts < 1793512800 else -5 * 3600)
    dow, hr = int(((x // 86400) + 3) % 7), (x % 86400) / 3600.0
    band = 74700 <= ts % 86400 <= 76500
    return dow == 4 and hr >= 14.0 and not band
rules.verdict: NOT SELECTIVE (beyond the existing band: test 1.46)

    dow, hr = int(((x // 86400) + 3) % 7), (x % 86400) / 3600.0
    band = 74700 <= ts % 86400 <= 76500
    return ((dow == 4 and hr >= 14.0) or (dow in (0, 1, 2, 3, 6) and 16.75 <= hr < 18.0)) and not band

rules.code:
def rule(t, A):
    """The US payrolls window: the FIRST Friday of the month, 08:00-09:30 New York (the market-correct version of pre_us_data). The day of
    the month comes from integer civil-date maths (no imports)."""
    ts = t["t_in"]
    x = ts + (-4 * 3600 if 1772953200 <= ts < 1793512800 else -5 * 3600)
    dow, hr = int(((x // 86400) + 3) % 7), (x % 86400) / 3600.0
    z = int(x // 86400) + 719468                                          # days -> civil date (H. Hinnant)
    era = (z if z >= 0 else z - 146096) // 146097
    doe = z - era * 146097
    yoe = (doe - doe // 1460 + doe // 36524 - doe // 146096) // 365
    doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe // 4 - yoe // 100)
    mp = (5 * doy + 2) // 153
    day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) // 5 + 1
    return dow == 4 and day <= 7 and 8.0 <= hr < 9.5
rules.verdict: NOT SELECTIVE (3 losers, insufficient n; train 1.75)

rules.code:
def rule(t, A):
    """The UHV level sits less than 1.0 pip short of a big figure (1.1200, 1.1300 ...) in the trade direction: the breakout must push
    through the resting orders at the figure to make even 0.1 pip + spread. Batch 8: 10-26 15:59 buy at 1.11996 (0.4 pip under 1.1200),
    10-09 sell at 1.12003 (0.3 pip above 1.1200)."""
    px, s, g = t["level"], t["side"], 0.01
    d = (math.ceil(px / g - 1e-9) * g - px) / 1e-4 if s > 0 else (px - math.floor(px / g + 1e-9) * g) / 1e-4
    return 0.0 < d <= 1.0

batch_notes:
HYPOTHESIS ONLY - NOT PROMOTED. Python tick replay; per CLAUDE.md only MT5's Strategy Tester (or live fills) may promote any of this. Lift and loss/win counts only, no win-rate or $ claims.
WHAT I SAW: all 22 charts + 44 twins. None of the 22 ever moved the 0.1 pip + spread the target needs (that is what a loss is here); 19 were full stop-outs and 3 forced weekly-close exits. The fill was the extreme of the next ~20 pips, so these are failed breakouts at the first tick. Read by eye, they look like double tops/floors, lower-high green humps, counter-structure x1 camels, climax re-tests and dead tapes. Every one of those ideas, coded and scored across all 7,626 trades, sits at lift 0.66-1.1: the twins carry the same picture. That covers equal highs/lows ahead, Zee's HH+HL camel fix (pivot and exact camel-replay versions), counter-trend, mature trend, shallow retracement, UHV = last candle, quiet market, breakout-minute pace and dip, efficiency ratio, spike nearby, and volume ratios. Two more were tested in pandas only: re-entry at the same level as an earlier trade within 15-120 min (about 1.0), and loss clustering after a recent loss (1.0-1.3).
WHAT SEPARATES: THE CLOCK. close_and_rollover (Friday after 14:00 New York OR Sun-Thu 16:45-18:00 New York) removes 26L/258W, lift 4.06 (train 4.14 / test 4.23).
RECOMMENDATION, in order: (1) The engine already has a switch, InpUhvNoClose (20:45-21:15 UTC). It is OFF in this setting (absent from the saved inputs). It should be redefined in New York time: the UTC band has been an hour early since US DST ended on 1 Nov, because the weekly close and rollover moved to ~22:00 UTC. (2) Beyond that band, the clock rule adds 15L/195W (train 3.59 / test 2.82). (3) The Friday>=14:00 NY part alone fails test beyond the band (1.46). The rollover part holds: 5L/45W (2.84/7.40), all real stop-outs. (4) 14 of the 18 Friday>=14 NY losers are FORCED weekly-close exits (why=8, partial losses), not stops. The Friday rule's value therefore depends on the MT5 EA flattening at the weekly close the way the sim does.
SECONDARY (fragile): big_figure_ahead (level <= 1 pip short of 1.1200/1.1300...) scores 7L/83W at 2.53/4.99. Beyond the clock it is 4L/79W at 1.99/1.88, found after ~50 grid variants, so it is a market-sensible hypothesis, not a result. fill_overshoot_15/20 (fill > 1.5/2 pips past the level) looks EXCELLENT raw but is mostly rollover spreads in disguise: beyond the clock only 3 losers.
BATCH 8: 2 losses are pure market close (10-09, 10-16), caught by EXCELLENT rules. 1 is the big figure (10-26 15:59). 4 more are caught only by the weaker fri_after_08ny (GOOD 2.21/2.88): the NFP sell on 10-02, the post-NFP sell on 10-02, the forced close on 10-23, and the pre-08:30-NY buy on 10-30. 15 are not caught by anything selective, and I say so plainly in each comment.
REGIME NOTE: the loss rate was ~4% in Mar-May, when the buy fill-over-level (spread proxy) was ~0.7 pip, and ~1.5% in Jun-Nov at ~0.2 pip. A 0.1-pip target is that sensitive to the broker spread, which is exactly why the MT5 run with real spreads decides.
